new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule for stress is given anywhere. The only first-hand published Buyu data (Meeussen's own field notes, published in his 1962 comparative tonology paper) mark every Buyu form for high vs low tone: roots contrast lexically (-sobol- L vs -kábu- H), and the subjunctive/imperative carry grammatical tone melodies (H prefix … H final -é; imperative with final H -á). Buyu is therefore treated as a tone language; stress is never mentioned.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Tonal notes: imperative plural suffix -wé (p. 34); tone-reversal languages show 'the opposite of Bembe and Buyu' (p. 27).
new_statements.domain_note: Verb forms only (subjunctive, subjunctive with infix, imperative sg./pl.), cited as isolated words from Meeussen's unpublished notes; not a phonological description of Buyu and not a statement about stress, word or phrase. The actual description (Meeussen 1951, Notes on Buyu, i+96 pp. ms., Tervuren) is not accessible.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog language-level buyu1239 (D55, ISO byi). Meeussen's data are labelled simply 'Buyu' from his own notes; the hh record for the 1951 ms. adds 'Pyana Mende = Penemendi = Buyu [byi]' (the Mende area of Kabambare territory). ALAC/Zaïre 1983 lists dialects kibujwé, kitwaga, kibuyu; the retired codes bmy 'Bemba/Kinyabemba' (bemb1258, bookkeeping) and sgo 'Songa' (song1304) were clan varieties of Buyu, not separate languages. No dialect is specified in the quoted source.
